title: Architectural Visualization for Urban Planning
business: Urban planning firms creating rapid visual prototypes for city council presentations.
problem: High-fidelity video generation often requires massive GPU clusters, leading to prohibitive costs and latency when iterating on simple site-plan concepts.
solution: Utilizing the Wan2.2-TI2V-5B-GGUF model allows firms to run high-quality text-to-video inference on local, consumer-grade hardware by leveraging quantized weights, significantly reducing infrastructure overhead.
steps: Select the appropriate GGUF quantization level based on available VRAM (e.g., Q4_K_M for a balance of quality and memory).
Configure the inference environment to support the specific 720P resolution requirements of 1280x704 or 704x1280.
Ensure the companion VAE (Wan2.2_VAE.safetensors) is loaded to handle the temporal compression requirements.
Input the scene description to generate the video clip, ensuring the frame count adheres to the 4k+1 constraint.
Validate the output against the architectural site plan for visual consistency.
outcome: The firm achieves faster iteration cycles for visual mockups, allowing stakeholders to review conceptual changes in real-time without cloud-based rendering delays.
limitation: The model is strictly limited to 720P resolution and specific aspect ratios; users must verify output dimensions and frame counts, as deviations will result in generation failures.
